issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: From Retrieval to Reasoning: Building Production-Ready Agentic AI Systems with Knowledge Graphs
author: Cassie Shum
description: Cassie Shum explains why knowledge graphs are a critical foundation for agentic systems. Moving beyond basic RAG, she explains four practical architectural patterns: context bundling, decision provenance, code as truth, and agent visibility, demonstrating an engineering harness to streamline feedback loops and maintain system reliability.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Beyond Offset Lag: Computing Time in Queue for Apache Hudi Data Lake Pipelines at Petabyte Scale
author: Srikanth Mamidala
description: Srikanth Mamidala explains how Twilio improved monitoring of its Kafka and Apache Hudi pipelines by complementing traditional offset lag with a time-in-queue metric that measures data staleness, enabling clearer visibility and early SLA warnings.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Your Next DSL Author Is a Language Model
author: Irakli Betchvaia
description: Irakli Betchvaia argues that LLMs struggle with domain-specific languages due to underrepresentation in training data, proposing Typed Domain Grounding—embedding DSLs in typed host languages like Kotlin or TypeScript so compilers catch syntax errors and repair output iteratively.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Platform Engineering in the Age of AI
author: InfoQ Live Panel
description: Panelists explore how internal platform teams adapt to support AI-assisted engineering workloads, balancing developer autonomy against standardization while establishing security guardrails, cost controls, and self-service capabilities.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Context Engineering at LinkedIn: How We Built an Organizational Context Layer for AI Agents with MCP
author: Ajay Prakash
description: Ajay Prakash discusses how LinkedIn overcomes AI agent limitations in large polyrepos using Contextual Agent Playbooks and Tools built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), serving procedural memory and code search to deliver 20% productivity gains.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: From S3 to GPU in One Copy: Rethinking Data Loading for ML Training
author: Onur Satici
description: Onur Satici introduces Vortex, an open-source columnar file format designed to stream data from cloud object storage directly to GPUs at up to 60 Gbps without upfront preprocessing, eliminating CPU and NVMe bottlenecks.

issue_title: Issue #110: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Implementing Durable Workflows on Postgres Without an External Orchestrator
author: Raman Varma
description: Case Study: Raman Varma details an architectural pattern to implement resilient, durable workflows natively within PostgreSQL using state machines and transactional boundaries, avoiding the operational overhead of external workflow engines.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Harper Argues against the Multi-System Stack and Releases 5.2
author: Renato Losio
description: The database platform Harper advocates for a single-runtime architecture that keeps application code and data together, with its benchmark against a Vercel-based stack reporting significantly better performance on live, personalized-data workloads, alongside a new record cache and higher throughput in version 5.2.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Spotify Builds External Index to Enable Low Latency Point Queries on its Data Lake
author: Leela Kumili
description: Spotify introduced Random Access Parquet (RAP), a storage architecture that facilitates writing low-latency point queries directly against data stored in its data lake, allowing online services and AI applications to retrieve individual records without replicating datasets into operational databases.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: Netflix Open-Sources Agentic Workflow for Causal Inference
author: Anthony Alford
description: Netflix open-sourced an agentic workflow for Observational Causal Inference (OCI) that reduces toil in causal analysis. Given observational data and the user's analysis plan, the agent uses an actor-critic loop to estimate causality, write a report, and suggest next steps.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: The Right 300 Tokens Beat 100k Noisy Ones: The Architecture of Context Engineering
author: Baruch Sadogursky & Patrick Debois
description: In this QCon London talk recording, Baruch Sadogursky and Patrick Debois discuss why coding agents fail due to bloated context windows and stuffed prompts. They explain practical context engineering fixes: lazy-loaded skills, versioned context artifacts, externalized memory banks, and LLM-as-a-judge evals.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: How Artificial Intelligence Disrupts Engineering Progression
author: Ben Linders
description: Alasdair Allan explains at QCon London how AI disrupts engineering career progression by eliminating learning opportunities at each rung while helping people perform above their experience level, slowing entry-level hiring and altering junior-to-senior team dynamics.

issue_title: Issue #109: Building Data and AI Platforms
title: An Evolutionary Architecture Pattern for Managing AI's Pace of Change
author: Joe Price, Branimir Đurek, Pavlos Migkiros & Trevor Dearham
description: Case Study: The authors propose the AI gateway as an architectural seam that isolates fast-moving parts of AI systems—guardrails, model routing, agent identity, action policy, and audit—allowing the underlying platform to remain stable amidst rapid model evolution.

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: Cloudflare Details Unified Data Platform Where Billing Workloads Account for 53% of Queries
author: Leela Kumili
description: Cloudflare detailed Town Lake, its internal unified data platform, and Skipper, an AI-powered analytics agent, unifying access to operational, billing, security, and business data previously fragmented across disparate systems.

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: Anthropic Reports Claude Now Handles 95% of Internal Analytics Queries
author: Renato Losio
description: Anthropic reports that Claude now handles 95% of its internal analytics requests, allowing employees to query business data independently by prioritizing rigorous data governance and semantic definitions over raw model size.

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: Neobank Monzo Builds Governed Data Mesh across 100 Teams and 12000 dbt Models
author: Renato Losio
description: Monzo redesigned its data warehouse into a governed, meshy architecture supporting over 100 teams and 12,000 dbt models, cutting warehouse operating costs by 40% while improving data delivery speed by 25%.

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: Challenging Google Analytics: Building a Scalable, Cost-Effective User Tracking Service
author: Alina Krasavina
description: In an InfoQ Dev Summit talk recording, Alina Krasavina explains how Delivery Hero deprecated Google Analytics to build an internal tracking service handling 10x more load and capturing 97% of tracking data with a simple, cost-effective distributed architecture.

metadata.theme: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: Compiling Workflows into Databases: the Architecture That Shouldn't Work (But Does)
author: Jeremy Edberg & Qian Li
description: Jeremy Edberg and Qian Li demonstrate DBOS Transact, showing how standard SQL tables, SKIP LOCKED queues, and unique primary keys can achieve durable workflow execution natively inside existing databases without external orchestrators.

issue_title: Issue #108: Building Data Platforms: Design, Architecture, and Enablement
title: From Batch to Micro-Batch Streaming: Lessons Learned the Hard Way in a Delta Index Pipeline
author: Parveen Saini
description: Case Study: Parveen Saini details the migration of a production ads and search delta-index pipeline from scheduled batch jobs to continuously running micro-batch streaming, cutting freshness lag from 10 minutes to 30 seconds.
